Bunun üstüne de final projesini duyururken bir haftamız gitti ve bu sizin yüzünüzden diyen Erhan hocamı unutmayacağım bu tutumundan dolayı. 29 Ekimin pazartesiye denk gelmesi mi suç tam olarak anlamadım. Ama bu istisnai durum haricinde iyi ki tanıştım dediğim hocalardan biridir. Ve inanıyorum ki bu tür mağdurluklar bir daha olmucak. Not: Bir projede süre uzatıldı ama 3 gün...

So much wasted time. So much of it. For a course with this many hours, we spend a huge chunk of it waiting around for feedback. We can’t even work in the meantime since they want to see the process and we’d have to redo it if they don't like it. There are two instructors. If they were to offer feedback separately we would save so much time, and yet for some reason, each critique session has to be a two-person event. They ask us to email the work for feedback if there wasn’t any time left in class, and proceeded to not reply to the mail. 

The feedbacks themselves feel dry as well. Mostly since the first weeks of a project seemingly is wasted by not actual work but convincing the instructors that we've done work. I understand why they ask for research, moodboards, all that... But not everyone has the same design process. Maybe it is a generational difference, but I don't need 30+ images from pinterest to visualize a concept. 5-6 is enough. I quite literally see thousands of images every day. Sometimes the inspiration is a mix of a video I've seen 2 years ago, a game I played as a kid, and an instagram ad I saw that morning. Most of the time we come up with the idea first, then find a couple pictures to help our instructors visualize it better. Not actually get inspired by the pictures themselves. Maybe their method is better, but to me and to most of my peers, it feels very unnatural.

course: Everything was SO SO much better than they were last semester. Separate sections are the way to go, we are too crowded for otherwise. Yes, we will graduate as designers, but that title is so much more diverse than it used to be. I think more artistic and symbolic approaches should be a little more welcome in our curriculum now, instead of the clear-cut, straight-to-the-point, over-analyzed, and excessively well-researched approach of graphic design. It makes the results much less creative and charming. It's okay to be a little ambiguous every now and then :) as a treat! Let's live a little.

instructor:
Ders stüdyo dersi fakat derste asla yaptığımız işin mantığı ya da teknik bilgi anlatılmadı. En fazla PDF'ten chapter okuyun gelin dendi. Ders feedback ağırlıklı ve ödevler üstünden yürüyor, ama feedbackler "Şurayı niye yaptın, olmuş mu bu sence? Al şunu şuraya koy." mantığında.

Çoğu derste ilk iki kişiye toplam 2 saat TÜRKÇE feedback verip kalan 10 küsür kişiye geri kalan 2 saati ayırıyor. Birbirimizin hatalarından öğrenmemiz gerektiğini vurguluyor sürekli, ancak yabancı uyruklu ve türkçe bilmeyen öğrenci olmasına rağmen dersi çoğunlukla TÜRKÇE yaptı, uyarıldığında ise 2-3 dakika ingilizce konuşup sonra tekrar Türkçe'ye dönüyor, hatasını hala düzeltemedi telafisi de yapılmadı.

instructor:
The instructor did not follow the offered syllabus, reduced the amount of classes from 3 per week down to 1 and was getting late. 
The insctructor has no clear objective about what he was teaching, so that by the end of the semester he had to do our homeworks by himself so that the whole class don't fail the course.

His manners were warm, respectful and he was very approachable. He was knowledgeable in his field and very open to help his students in improving their work. He was adaptable to situations at hand and handled arising problems or confusions with patience and care. I think there were problems planning-wise. The time we had during classes wasn't used as effectively as it could've been because the tasks at hand weren't defined too clearly. This confusion could have been avoided if the students were more clearly briefed about what was expected and about the resources we could use throughout the class early on the semester.

It is probably because of the mess the Covid19 has created but, I don't feel like the lecture in general was organized beforehand. The assignments were not evaluated properly. There was (and still is) a rush to finish things up before the grading period begin. I don't think  as students we understood what we were supposed to do during the time of this lecture from the beginning of this semester. We have a hard time now trying to put something out there and receive a good grade with our final product. Even our projects don't feel complete or in any way "good" for us because of the poor time management. I blame it partially on the poor levels of communication between us students and the instructor. The other half of the fault belongs to the person who thought it would be a good idea to open up this course during this pandemic.

He had a poor time management. He didn't offer a well structured syllabus, the syllabus we have used indicated nothing. The term projects were last minute projects because of the poor knowledge we have had about the course contents. He taught only the basics of Max, a visual programming language we might use for our term project. He provided us with examples of projects, patches and so on but explanation of them was lacking. I am strongly disappointed in taking this class, which at the first glance offered an amazing content.
course: The course's syllabus had potential and could contribute my portfolio for PhD application but it was not followed so I consider the class as a failure.

The syllabus was really interesting and exciting. I learned a lot about a field I am relatively new to. However, we steered away from the syllabus a little too much at times. Our time wasn't managed effectively and we didn't get to produce the things we could've produced. But, I think for this class, the blame could partially be put on the online method. Because the content of the class could have been utilized much more if we had a physical space we could work in together.

Since the course is mostly about installations, there wasn't much to do... We are in a pandemic. We tried to shift the final projects from physical structures to web based individual projects but I don't think that worked well. I only took this course because I had very limited options but I was optimistic about it, I was actually very excited. It is a pity that my excitement turned into anxiety over the weeks because of the course topics. I don't think starting to learn a new software/program after the first month of the semester was a good idea. We didn't even get to use what we have learned in our final projects. I knew this course was an mfa course so we weren't going to write much but create instead. However, I would have preferred to write a report or a paper over preparing a project I don't even have the full control of. I am very unhappy considering I literally didn't learn anything that would be useful to me in the future. If this course is going to be available to others in future semesters, I have a suggestion... The final project/assignment needs to be a stable and creative one so there can be an option given to students; either do a creative project or write a final paper on a topic the instructor also approves. I personally don't see a point why this class was even available for us in the first place, during a pandemic.
The idea of the course is great. It is good that Bilkent is offering a course like that. But it's very poorly structured and it lacked so many things.
